name: Water Ripple Image
rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; click-driven concentric rings with a refraction read make it distinct from ripple-distortion's pointer-move noise, and masked clones replace WebGL so it ships dependency-free on any media.

radius.description: Radius a ring reaches by the end of its life, in px.

duration.description: Lifetime of one ring, in ms.

spacing.description: Delay between the rings of one drop, in ms.

strength.description: Peak refraction: how far a crest magnifies (and a trough shrinks) the image.

band.description: Half-width of a ring band, in px.

glint.description: How much a crest brightens and a trough darkens.

maxDrops.description: Drops alive at once; the oldest is cleared first.

autoDrip.description: Drop at a random spot every this many ms while on screen; 0 turns it off.

a11y: Every ring is an aria-hidden, inert clone of the media with its ids stripped, so screen readers meet the image's label once and no cloned link or control can take focus.
Rings ignore pointer events and nothing calls preventDefault, so a click still reaches any link or control inside the host.
The host is not made focusable: the ripple is decoration only and never carries information.
Reduced motion (at mount or changed live) clears every ring, stops the loop and ignores clicks; forced-colors mode hides the rings.
